B121.title: Watch holds rechecks until the block join
B121.note: Watch mode queues a file's first commit at once; later commits of a file that already has a ticket are held (watch.held row) until review-file --wait-block queues one ticket for the latest content. Stops a half-done fix commit from using the file's review rounds.

B106.title: Worker registry: one announcement per worker
B106.note: Each worker writes <repo>/.code-forge/workers/<pid>-<start_time>.json next to worker.json and beats both; boot counts live entries and announces under one cross-process lock (limit 1); boot prunes dead entries (known start-time mismatch = dead); an unreadable entry blocks boot and doctor lists it; liveWorker keeps the B30 fresh-heartbeat rule.

B122.title: Join delivers unseen findings before a recheck
B122.note: At review-file --wait-block, a file whose newest review found problems and that changed after it (a commit made blind to the findings) is not rechecked: the join answers status findings with that ticket and writes one delivered marker. The next join rechecks the latest content once. Stops a blind commit from counting as a stall round.

B123.title: Reopen clears old cap ids after a fresh review
B123.note: A review.cap row is superseded when a verified human review.reopened row comes after it and then a signed review.round of the file's current content. A superseded cap row adds no ids to the close check, so after a reopen only the fresh review's own findings need a fix, waiver or answer.

B126.title: Leak test ignores files already in the repo's .code-forge
B126.note: The final-check test in orphan.test.mjs forged an empty baseline, so files already in the repo's .code-forge folder (normal when code-forge builds itself) showed up as leaks and failed npm test. The test now records the folder's current contents as the baseline and still checks the exact planted leak list.

B125.title: The join reruns a stale review of the current content once
B125.note: review-file --wait-block: when the ticket of a file's current content is done with a result that never counted (stale, unavailable, round-1 split_required), the join drops that done marker with the --fresh claim and the worker reviews the content once; at most one drop per ticket, kept on disk. Counted results are never dropped.

B124a.title: block waive --yes: an evidence-backed agent waiver a fresh judge must agree with
B124a.note: block waive --yes skips the terminal confirm only for a finding whose signed recorded severity is warning or nit; the reason must cite evidence (path:line, a test file, or an acceptance clause); a fresh L3 judge must agree; then one signed review.waived row by: agent with the verdict. Critical or unknown severity is refused waive-yes-critical; no evidence waive-yes-no-evidence (judge not called); disagree waive-yes-disagreed. The gate counts an agreed agent waiver; block close lists agent waivers and --json adds agent_waivers. block reopen stays human-only with no --yes.

B127.title: block accept-hit: the human accepts one named false transcript hit
B127.note: block accept-hit <id> --run --rule --line --transcript --reason: human-only (terminal yes, no --yes); pre-checks refuse accept-hit-no-such-hit before any prompt when the transcript scan does not report that (rule, line); on yes one signed rule_break.accepted row {block, rule, line, line_sha256, reason, by: human}. block close drops a transcript hit only when a verified accepted row of the same run and block has the same rule and the sha256 of that exact line text; a rule_break ledger row is never accepted. close prints each accepted hit; --json adds accepted_hits. The verb is coder-only forbidden.

B124b.title: undo and audit agent waivers: block unwaive, report agent_waivers, require_ack + block ack-waivers
B124b.note: block unwaive <id> <finding> --run --file --reason: human-only; refuses unwaive-no-agent-waiver before any prompt unless a verified by: agent waiver exists; writes a signed review.unwaived row that cancels earlier agent waivers of that (block, file, finding) on the gate and the review-file pre-check. report gets a 15th section agent_waivers {block, file, finding, severity, reason, verdict, unwaived}. review.agent_waivers.require_ack (frozen at run start): close refuses agent-waivers-not-acked until a human block ack-waivers row matches the digest of the counted agent waivers; ack-waivers-none with none. Both verbs are coder-only forbidden.

B124c.title: agent reopen: block reopen --yes with evidence, fresh judge, one per block and file per run; close audit agent_reopens
B124c.note: block reopen <id> --file --reason --yes: the reason must cite evidence (reopen-yes-no-evidence), a fresh judge must agree (reopen-yes-disagreed), at most one agent reopen per block and file per run (reopen-yes-limit); the row is by: agent. An agreed, verified agent reopen supersedes the B123 cap like a human reopen. block close --json lists agent_reopens. Without --yes the verb still needs human confirmation.

B128.title: CI green on Linux Node 22 and 24: test isolation flag both versions accept; claim fixture publishes its counts atomically
B128.note: Root cause: the claim fixture created its completion file before it wrote the count, so a Linux inotify wake could read an empty file as 0. Write to a temp file and rename. Node 22.23 rejects --test-isolation=none; use --experimental-test-isolation=none.

B130.title: README for new users; per-version history lives only in CHANGELOG; release updates only the Latest line
B130.note: README went from 474 to 171 lines: pitch, problem, install, quickstart, how it works, commands, agents, security, links (incl. public roadmap). Release no longer moves README bullets.

B129.title: upgrade prints an ASCII code-forge logo, the version change and what's new; --plain for scripts
B129.note: Install records get an optional version field. Summary: logo, 'code-forge <v>', '<old> -> <new>' / 'already on' / 'first versioned upgrade', kept record lines, first 5 CHANGELOG bullets, 'Full notes: <path>'.

B131.title: Budget split counts removed lines; Markdown steps up to full; join reports an outcome per file and queues owned files with no ticket
B131.note: split_required only above full_in; --wait-block files carry outcome (approved/findings/stopped/split_required/unavailable/null); split_required gives done:false with reason and next.

B132.title: A lens budget change reruns a split_required stop for the lens that was measured
B132.note: F2: --fresh re-queues a counted split_required stop when its lens budget changed; the stop keeps its real lens (full, recheck or patch_check).
